days with the combination of forest fire and water scarcity advisory in the period 2011-
2020. 
 
average more than 400 warnings issued per year. Also, warnings of strong wind 
gusts and high ocean level were issued more than 200 times per year on average. 
• Advisories, except high temperature advisories (NumDD = 299), were more 
frequently issued when compared with the different types of warnings, with on 
average ≥1000 advisories issued per year (i.e., 1746 times for water scarcity, 
1386 times for forest fire and 966 times for grassland fire).   
• From December to March, high river flow warnings were mainly issued for 
districts in southern Sweden with a relatively high number along the south and 
west coasts. From April on, the same type of risk spread towards the north, where 
high river flow warnings occurred much more often in comparison with the rest 
of the country and reached the annual peak from May to July in connection with 
the spring flood. For the rest of the year high flow warnings were issued but with 
fewer numbers in general.   
• Heavy rainfall warnings mainly occurred from May to October. July-October is 
the period in which the majority of the country is affected by heavy rainfall. 
Higher-than-normal number of warnings were issued particularly in August and 
particularly for districts along the east coast in northern Sweden and the west 
coast in southern Sweden. 
• Heavy snowfall warnings were often issued with on average 1-2 days in at least 
one district per month from November to March, in particular in December (e.g., 
Västernorrland and the coastal area of Västerbotten with >5 warning days on 
average) and January (e.g., central part of Sweden with >4 warning days on 
average). 
• The risk of water scarcity in watercourses mainly appeared in the central and 
southern part of Sweden from June to December. In particular, the south-eastern 
districts Södermanland, Östergötland and Kalmar appear as more risk prone 
regions where the number of days with issued advisories reached high during 
July and August.  
• Year 2018 was the year with a record-high number of issued forest fire 
advisories, water scarcity advisories and high temperature warning. It was also 

===== PAGE 39 =====
 
 34 
the year with the second highest number of issued high river flow warnings, 
likely due to relatively heavy snowfall in winter 2017-2018.  
The main findings for double (overlapping) WAs are summarized in the following, with 
focus on hydrology and warnings: 
• Concerning two overlapping warnings, the districts along the west coast (i.e., 
Bohuslän and Göteborg, Halland and Skåne utom Österlen) and the north-east 
coast (i.e., Västerbottens kustland and Norrbottens kustland) were most affected, 
in particular during winter (December-February).  
• The most common combination according to metrics NumDD and NumDays was 
high ocean level together with strong wind gusts. The two single warnings 
included showed fairly high inter-annual variability.  
• The main warning combination including hydrology was that of high river flow 
and strong wind gusts, which showed up high in all metrics. The most affected 
districts are located along the west coast in southern Sweden, where the 
combination occurred up to once per month in in February and December. 
• Concerning the combination of one warning and one advisory, the districts along 
the south-eastern coast in July and August were found most affected, followed by 
the districts along the north-east coast. High river flow warning combined with 
grassland fire advisory ia a hydrology-related multiple hazard that came up high 
in all metrics. 
• The combination between water scarcity and forest fire stands out as the most 
frequent combination of two advisories.  
The overlap between high river flow and heavy rainfall warnings came up high in terms 
of affected districts (NumDistricts and AvgDistricts) and thus normally affected large 
areas. It appeared from May to October but with low frequency, less than day per month. 
It is especially “hydrologically problematic”, as when high river flow coincides with 
heavy rainfall, simultaneously or successively, the infrastructure may be damaged or 
corresponding preparedness is inadequate in case the combined risk is overlooked. Three 
regions were found associated with relatively high risk: (1) the western coastal districts in 
October, (2) central Sweden in May and (3) northern Sweden in July. 
Also, the combination between high river flow and high ocean level deserves to be 
mentioned and described as a notable warning combination, as it comes up quite high in 
terms of both NumDD and NumDays. It is also hydrologically problematic in coastal 
regions, where total water levels may be influenced by both processes. The consideration 
of this type of double WA is important for designing flood protection infrastructure and 
drainage in affected regions. In Sweden, it mainly occurs in the districts along the west 
and south coast (October to March), the south-east coast (January and February) and the 
north-east coast (June, October and November). The results show that Halland, Bohuslän 
and Göteborg in Västra Götaland and Skåne län utom Österlen were the most influenced 
with a ferquency >4 times/year. Especially, in February in Skåne län utom Österlen the 
monthly occurrence is almost twice per month.  
The double WA of high river flow warning and grassland fire advisory starts from 
southern Sweden with relatively high risk in March and then spreads northward to 
northern Sweden. The highest risk appeared in May, with up to seven days per month for 
the coastal district in Norrbotten. April is a hotspot month, as nearly all of Sweden has 
experienced this double WA in April, except in the south-western regions and in the 
mountain chain. This WA was found to often affect large areas and it is likely to occur 
due to snow melt from February to June.  
As mentioned above, water scarcity shows a strong link to the forest fire hazard with 
frequent overlap. This combination of advisories normally starts in June and ends by 

===== PAGE 40 =====
 
35 
 
October, peaking during the summer months (June-August). July stands out as the month 
when this double WA were active in most of Sweden, except in the mountain chain and in 
the very north. In particular the districts in south-eastern Sweden are a hotspot where the 
frequency of occurrence exceeds half the month in July and August.  
To conclude, exploring the spatio-temporal distributions of warnings and advisories is a 
way to identify risk-prone regions and seasons. This may help municipalities and rescue 
services to make up infrastructure plans and precaution strategies so as to maximize the 
capability and avoid potential disasters. Furthermore, the results may be used as a basis to 
identify topics of special interests for different purposes, e.g., acquire a deeper 
understanding of the involved processes, develop tailored indicators, etc.  
The results show that high river flow and high ocean level are often one of the single 
hazards involved in overlapping combinations (double WAs) in a Swedish context. They 
may co-occur with other single hazards such as strong wind gusts, heavy snowfall, etc., 
and trigger different kinds of compound events causing a stronger-than-expected impact. 
Also, more attention should be given to advisories of forest fire and water scarcity, that 
are frequently issued. 
As the climate varies naturally from one year to the next, sufficiently long time series 
(i.e., ≥30 years) are always required in order to capture different kinds of forcing that may 
have effects on climate system. The limited length of data on warnings and advisories in 
this study (10 years) means that we cannot draw any firm conclusions in terms of how 
certain parts of Sweden are affected by different kinds of natural hazards and their 
combinations, only find indications. Thus, the presented results, e.g. in terms of regional 
patterns, are to some extent affected by samling uncertainties. 
Further research is needed confirm the findings in this report as well as to focus on 
different multiple and/or compound events in order to deepen the knowledge of the 
underlying physical processes and driving forces. Model data such as ensemble forecasts 
and climate projection can be used for assessment on different time horizons, aiming at 
developing early warnings and alerts as well as estimating changes in frequency, severity 
and seasonality of multiple hazards. We believe such efforts should be a key component 
in analyses for adaptation towards a climate-proof society.

APPENDIX A 
Analysis of durations of single WAs 
 
As described in section 4.1, the WAs extracted from the KEPS system contained short-
lived, “false” WAs that were just updates of an existing WA and not a new WA. To 
eliminate as many as possible of the false WAs, it was decided to use a lower “duration 
threshold” below which a WA is considered false. Figure A1 illustrate how the false WAs 
influence the distributions (histograms) of single natural hazards’ durations at sub-daily 
scale. They show the total number of entries in the KEPS outtake 2011-2020 of any class 
of the type of warning, for durations between 0 and 24 hours. 
 
As the data will be aggregated to a daily scale, the first step is to construct a matrix 
𝐴𝑡𝑐
𝑑 (𝑖, 𝑗) of all active warnings of type t and class c on day i in district j, of a duration 
longer than the duration threshold d. To study the impact of the threshold d, the KEPS 
outtake was traversed and if the duration of an entry is more than d=0, 1, 2, etc., hours, 
𝐴𝑡𝑐
𝑑 (𝑖, 𝑗) is increased by 1 for the districts and days where it was active. Table A1 shows 
the sum of 𝐴𝑡𝑐
𝑑 (𝑖, 𝑗) over all days, districts and classes for d=1 to 12 hours.  
 
The analysis then uses the indicator matrix Stc(i,j) (section 4.2.1), which is 1 if 𝐴𝑡𝑐
𝑑 (𝑖, 𝑗)>0 
and 0 otherwise. Table A2 shows the sum of Stc(i,j) over all days, districts and classes of 
each WA type (this is metric NumDD summed over all classes). Some WA types have a 
large difference between Table A1 and A2, e.g. high river flow has a sum that is almost 
twice as high in Table A1. This is mainly because those warnings are extended on most 
days and then produce two active warnings in a day in KEPS, although it is the same 
warning. 
 
The bars in figure A1 are approximately the difference between two adjacent columns in 
Table A1 and is more loosely related to the difference between the columns of Table A2. 
As can be seen in the histograms and Table A2, warnings related to slow processes like 
high river flow and high temperature are fairly independent of the duration threshold at a 
sub-daily scale from one or a few hours and up. The meteorological warnings have a 
much more gradual decay. 
 
To choose a single duration threshold for all WAs means to strike a balance between two 
risks; on one hand including too many suspicious warnings for types associated with slow 
processes, and on the other hand excluding too many “true” warnings for short-lived 
meteorological hazards. From the sums in Table A2, a duration threshold of 2 hours 
appears to be appropriate as (1) the number of WAs of slow processes stabilizes for 
longer durations and (2) most of the numbers associated with short-lived WAs have not 
started to decay sharply. The 2-hour duration threshold was also discussed and agreed 
with the reviewers of the report, and we believe that the final indicator matrix Stc(i,j) well 
reflect the spatio-temporal characteristics of only true warnings.

    55→def load_training_data(path: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    56→    """Load merged training data (MESAN features + snow depth)."""
    57→    path = Path(path)
    58→
    59→    # Try parquet first
    60→    if path.with_suffix('.parquet').exists():
    61→        logger.info(f"Loading from {path.with_suffix('.parquet')}")
    62→        df = pd.read_parquet(path.with_suffix('.parquet'))
    63→    elif path.exists():
    64→        logger.info(f"Loading from {path}")
    65→        df = pd.read_csv(path)
    66→    else:
    67→        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Training data not found at {path}")
    68→
    69→    df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'])
    70→    df['station_id'] = df['station_id'].astype(str)
    71→
    72→    logger.info(f"  Rows: {len(df):,}")
    73→    logger.info(f"  Stations: {df['station_id'].nunique()}")
    74→    logger.info(f"  Date range: {df['date'].min().date()} to {df['date'].max().date()}")
    75→    logger.info(f"  Columns: {list(df.columns)}")
    76→
    77→    return df
    78→
    79→
    80→def filter_winter_months(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    81→    """Keep only winter months (Oct-Apr)."""
    82→    before = len(df)
    83→    df = df[df['date'].dt.month.isin(WINTER_MONTHS)].copy()
    84→    logger.info(f"  Winter filter: {before:,} -> {len(df):,} rows")
    85→    return df
    86→
    87→
    88→def check_station_continuity(
    89→    df: pd.DataFrame,
    90→    min_days: int = 38,
    91→    max_gap_days: int = 3
    92→) -> pd.DataFrame:
    93→    """
    94→    Filter to contiguous segments with enough days for sequence creation.
    95→
    96→    A station needs at least seq_length + forecast_horizon + 1 consecutive
    97→    days to produce even one training sequence. Gaps > max_gap_days break
    98→    continuity.
    99→    """
   100→    logger.info(f"Checking station continuity (min {min_days} days, max gap {max_gap_days} days)...")
   101→
   102→    good_segments = []
   103→    stations = df['station_id'].unique()
   104→    dropped_stations = 0
   105→    total_segments = 0
   106→
   107→    for station_id in stations:
   108→        sdf = df[df['station_id'] == station_id].sort_values('date')
   109→
   110→        if len(sdf) < min_days:
   111→            dropped_stations += 1
   112→            continue
   113→
   114→        # Find gaps that break continuity
   115→        dates = sdf['date'].values
   116→        diffs = np.diff(dates).astype('timedelta64[D]').astype(int)
   117→        gap_indices = np.where(diffs > max_gap_days)[0]
   118→
   119→        # Split into contiguous segments
   120→        segments = np.split(np.arange(len(sdf)), gap_indices + 1)
   121→
   122→        station_has_good_segment = False
   123→        for seg in segments:
   124→            if len(seg) >= min_days:
   125→                good_segments.append(sdf.iloc[seg])
   126→                total_segments += 1
   127→                station_has_good_segment = True
   128→
   129→        if not station_has_good_segment:
   130→            dropped_stations += 1
   131→
   132→    if not good_segments:
   133→        raise ValueError("No stations have enough contiguous data for sequence creation")
   134→
   135→    result = pd.concat(good_segments, ignore_index=True)
   136→    n_stations = result['station_id'].nunique()
   137→
   138→    logger.info(f"  Stations with sufficient continuity: {n_stations} / {len(stations)}")
   139→    logger.info(f"  Stations dropped: {dropped_stations}")
   140→    logger.info(f"  Contiguous segments: {total_segments}")
   141→    logger.info(f"  Rows retained: {len(result):,}")
   142→
   143→    return result
   144→

   146→def prepare_dataset(
   147→    training_data_path: str = "data/processed/training_data.csv",
   148→    config_path: str = "configs/multitask_mesan.yaml",
   149→    output_dir: str = "data/processed",
   150→    winter_only: bool = True
   151→) -> None:
   152→    """
   153→    Full dataset preparation pipeline.
   154→
   155→    1. Load merged training data
   156→    2. Optionally filter to winter months
   157→    3. Check station continuity
   158→    4. Split by year (train/val/test)
   159→    5. Fit preprocessor on training data
   160→    6. Create per-station sequences for each split
   161→    7. Save as .npz files + metadata
   162→    """
   163→    output_dir = Path(output_dir)
   164→    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   165→
   166→    # Load config
   167→    logger.info("Loading config...")
   168→    config = load_config(config_path)
   169→    data_cfg = config['data']
   170→
   171→    features = data_cfg.get('features', FEATURES_MESAN)
   172→    snow_col = data_cfg.get('snow_col', SNOW_DEPTH_COL)
   173→    seq_length = data_cfg.get('seq_length', 30)
   174→    forecast_horizon = data_cfg.get('forecast_horizon', 7)
   175→    train_years = tuple(data_cfg.get('train_years', [2015, 2022]))
   176→    val_year = data_cfg.get('val_year', 2023)
   177→    test_year = data_cfg.get('test_year', 2024)
   178→
   179→    logger.info(f"  Features ({len(features)}): {features}")
   180→    logger.info(f"  Snow col: {snow_col}")
   181→    logger.info(f"  Seq length: {seq_length}, Forecast horizon: {forecast_horizon}")
   182→    logger.info(f"  Split: train {train_years}, val {val_year}, test {test_year}")
   183→
   184→    # --- Load data ---
   185→    logger.info("")
   186→    logger.info("=" * 60)
   187→    logger.info("STEP 1: Load training data")
   188→    logger.info("=" * 60)
   189→    df = load_training_data(training_data_path)
   190→
   191→    # --- Winter filter ---
   192→    if winter_only:
   193→        logger.info("")
   194→        logger.info("=" * 60)
   195→        logger.info("STEP 2: Filter to winter months (Oct-Apr)")
   196→        logger.info("=" * 60)
   197→        df = filter_winter_months(df)
   198→
   199→    # --- Continuity check ---
   200→    logger.info("")
   201→    logger.info("=" * 60)
   202→    logger.info("STEP 3: Check station continuity")
   203→    logger.info("=" * 60)
   204→    min_days = seq_length + forecast_horizon + 1
   205→    df = check_station_continuity(df, min_days=min_days)
   206→
   207→    # --- Split by year ---
   208→    logger.info("")
   209→    logger.info("=" * 60)
   210→    logger.info("STEP 4: Temporal split")
   211→    logger.info("=" * 60)
   212→    train_df, val_df, test_df = create_train_val_test_split(
   213→        df, train_years=train_years, val_year=val_year, test_year=test_year
   214→    )
   215→
   216→    for name, split_df in [('Train', train_df), ('Val', val_df), ('Test', test_df)]:
   217→        if len(split_df) == 0:
   218→            logger.warning(f"  {name} split is EMPTY! Check year range and data availability.")
   219→        else:
   220→            logger.info(f"  {name} stations: {split_df['station_id'].nunique()}")
   221→
   222→    # --- Fit preprocessor ---
   223→    logger.info("")
   224→    logger.info("=" * 60)
   225→    logger.info("STEP 5: Fit preprocessor on training data")
   226→    logger.info("=" * 60)
   227→    preprocessor = SnowDataPreprocessor(
   228→        seq_length=seq_length,
   229→        forecast_horizon=forecast_horizon,
   230→        features=features,
   231→        snow_col=snow_col
   232→    )
   233→    preprocessor.fit(train_df)
   234→
   235→    # Report scaler stats
   236→    feature_cols = [c for c in features if c in train_df.columns]
   237→    logger.info(f"  Scaler fitted on {len(feature_cols)} features")
   238→    for i, feat in enumerate(feature_cols):
   239→        logger.info(f"    {feat:20s}: mean={preprocessor.scaler.mean_[i]:8.2f}, "
   240→                     f"std={preprocessor.scaler.scale_[i]:8.2f}")
   241→
   242→    # Save preprocessor
   243→    preprocessor_dir = output_dir / 'preprocessor'
   244→    preprocessor.save(str(preprocessor_dir))
   245→    logger.info(f"  Preprocessor saved to {preprocessor_dir}")
   246→
   247→    # --- Create sequences ---
   248→    logger.info("")
   249→    logger.info("=" * 60)
   250→    logger.info("STEP 6: Create per-station sequences")
   251→    logger.info("=" * 60)
   252→
   253→    metadata = {
   254→        'seq_length': seq_length,
   255→        'forecast_horizon': forecast_horizon,
   256→        'n_features': len(feature_cols),
   257→        'features': feature_cols,
   258→        'snow_col': snow_col,
   259→        'train_years': list(train_years),
   260→        'val_year': val_year,
   261→        'test_year': test_year,
   262→        'winter_only': winter_only
   263→    }
   264→
   265→    splits = {'train': train_df, 'val': val_df, 'test': test_df}
   266→    for split_name, split_df in splits.items():
   267→        if len(split_df) == 0:
   268→            logger.warning(f"  Skipping {split_name} (empty)")
   269→            metadata[f'{split_name}_samples'] = 0
   270→            continue
   271→
   272→        logger.info(f"")
   273→        logger.info(f"  Processing {split_name} split ({len(split_df):,} rows, "
   274→                     f"{split_df['station_id'].nunique()} stations)...")
   275→        data_dict = preprocessor.transform(split_df, create_sequences=True)
   276→
   277→        n_seq = len(data_dict['input'])
   278→        n_anomaly = int(data_dict['target_D'].sum())
   279→        pct = n_anomaly / n_seq * 100 if n_seq > 0 else 0
   280→
   281→        logger.info(f"    Sequences:    {n_seq:,}")
   282→        logger.info(f"    Input shape:  {data_dict['input'].shape}")
   283→        logger.info(f"    Target A:     mean={data_dict['target_A'].mean():.1f}, "
   284→                     f"std={data_dict['target_A'].std():.1f}, "
   285→                     f"max={data_dict['target_A'].max():.1f} cm")
   286→        logger.info(f"    Target B:     shape {data_dict['target_B'].shape}")
   287→        logger.info(f"    Anomaly:      {n_anomaly} positive ({pct:.1f}%)")
   288→
   289→        # Save
   290→        out_path = output_dir / f'{split_name}_sequences.npz'
   291→        np.savez_compressed(
   292→            out_path,
   293→            input=data_dict['input'],
   294→            target_A=data_dict['target_A'],
   295→            target_B=data_dict['target_B'],
   296→            target_D=data_dict['target_D']
   297→        )
   298→        size_mb = out_path.stat().st_size / (1024 * 1024)
   299→        logger.info(f"    Saved to {out_path} ({size_mb:.1f} MB)")
   300→
   301→        # Store metadata
   302→        metadata[f'{split_name}_samples'] = n_seq
   303→        metadata[f'{split_name}_anomaly_rate'] = float(data_dict['target_D'].mean())
   304→
   305→    # Save metadata
   306→    meta_path = output_dir / 'metadata.json'
   307→    with open(meta_path, 'w') as f:
   308→        json.dump(metadata, f, indent=2)
   309→    logger.info(f"  Metadata saved to {meta_path}")
   310→
   311→    # --- Summary ---
   312→    logger.info("")
   313→    logger.info("=" * 60)
   314→    logger.info("DATASET PREPARATION SUMMARY")
   315→    logger.info("=" * 60)
   316→    for split_name in ['train', 'val', 'test']:
   317→        npz_path = output_dir / f'{split_name}_sequences.npz'
   318→        if npz_path.exists():
   319→            data = np.load(npz_path)
   320→            logger.info(f"  {split_name:5s}: {data['input'].shape[0]:>8,} sequences, "
   321→                         f"input {data['input'].shape}, "
   322→                         f"size {npz_path.stat().st_size / (1024*1024):.1f} MB")
   323→        else:
   324→            logger.info(f"  {split_name:5s}: NOT CREATED")
   325→
   326→    logger.info(f"  Features ({len(feature_cols)}): {feature_cols}")
   327→    logger.info(f"  Preprocessor: {preprocessor_dir}")
   328→    logger.info("")
   329→    logger.info("Ready for training with:")
   330→    logger.info(f"  python train.py --config {config_path}")

     8→class SpatialHead(nn.Module):
     9→    """
    10→    Head A: Spatial snow depth prediction.
    11→
    12→    Predicts current snow depth given encoded weather/snow features.
    13→
    14→    Args:
    15→        input_size: Size of encoder output
    16→        hidden_size: Size of hidden layer
    17→        dropout: Dropout probability
    18→    """
    19→
    20→    def __init__(
    21→        self,
    22→        input_size: int = 128,
    23→        hidden_size: int = 64,
    24→        dropout: float = 0.2
    25→    ):
    26→        super().__init__()
    27→
    28→        self.network = nn.Sequential(
    29→            nn.Linear(input_size, hidden_size),
    30→            nn.ReLU(),
    31→            nn.Dropout(dropout),
    32→            nn.Linear(hidden_size, hidden_size // 2),
    33→            nn.ReLU(),
    34→            nn.Dropout(dropout),
    35→            nn.Linear(hidden_size // 2, 1)
    36→        )
    37→
    38→    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    39→        """
    40→        Forward pass.
    41→
    42→        Args:
    43→            x: Encoder output (batch_size, input_size)
    44→
    45→        Returns:
    46→            Predicted snow depth (batch_size, 1)
    47→        """
    48→        return self.network(x)

    51→class TemporalHead(nn.Module):
    52→    """
    53→    Head B: Temporal forecasting (7-day ahead prediction).
    54→
    55→    Uses LSTM decoder to generate multi-step forecasts.
    56→
    57→    Args:
    58→        input_size: Size of encoder output
    59→        hidden_size: Size of decoder hidden state
    60→        forecast_horizon: Number of days to forecast
    61→        dropout: Dropout probability
    62→    """
    63→
    64→    def __init__(
    65→        self,
    66→        input_size: int = 128,
    67→        hidden_size: int = 64,
    68→        forecast_horizon: int = 7,
    69→        dropout: float = 0.2
    70→    ):
    71→        super().__init__()
    72→
    73→        self.forecast_horizon = forecast_horizon
    74→        self.hidden_size = hidden_size
    75→
    76→        # Project encoder output to decoder input
    77→        self.input_projection = nn.Linear(input_size, hidden_size)
    78→
    79→        # LSTM decoder
    80→        self.decoder_lstm = nn.LSTM(
    81→            input_size=hidden_size,
    82→            hidden_size=hidden_size,
    83→            num_layers=1,
    84→            batch_first=True,
    85→            dropout=0
    86→        )
    87→
    88→        # Output layer
    89→        self.output_layer = nn.Sequential(
    90→            nn.Linear(hidden_size, hidden_size // 2),
    91→            nn.ReLU(),
    92→            nn.Dropout(dropout),
    93→            nn.Linear(hidden_size // 2, 1)
    94→        )
    95→
    96→    def forward(
    97→        self,
    98→        encoder_output: torch.Tensor,
    99→        encoder_hidden: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
   100→    ) -> torch.Tensor:
   101→        """
   102→        Forward pass for temporal forecasting.
   103→
   104→        Args:
   105→            encoder_output: Encoder context (batch_size, input_size)
   106→            encoder_hidden: Optional LSTM hidden state from encoder
   107→
   108→        Returns:
   109→            Forecasted snow depths (batch_size, forecast_horizon)
   110→        """
   111→        batch_size = encoder_output.size(0)
   112→
   113→        # Project encoder output
   114→        decoder_input = self.input_projection(encoder_output)
   115→
   116→        # Repeat for each forecast step
   117→        decoder_input = decoder_input.unsqueeze(1).repeat(1, self.forecast_horizon, 1)
   118→        # Shape: (batch, forecast_horizon, hidden_size)
   119→
   120→        # Decode
   121→        decoder_output, _ = self.decoder_lstm(decoder_input)
   122→        # Shape: (batch, forecast_horizon, hidden_size)
   123→
   124→        # Generate predictions
   125→        predictions = self.output_layer(decoder_output)
   126→        # Shape: (batch, forecast_horizon, 1)
   127→
   128→        return predictions.squeeze(-1)  # (batch, forecast_horizon)

   131→class TemporalHeadMLP(nn.Module):
   132→    """
   133→    Simplified temporal head using MLP instead of LSTM decoder.
   134→
   135→    Maps the encoder context vector directly to forecast_horizon outputs.
   136→    Fewer parameters than the LSTM decoder, reducing overfitting risk.
   137→
   138→    Args:
   139→        input_size: Size of encoder output
   140→        hidden_size: Size of hidden layer
   141→        forecast_horizon: Number of days to forecast
   142→        dropout: Dropout probability
   143→        n_layers: Number of linear layers (1-4). Default 2 matches original.
   144→    """
   145→
   146→    def __init__(
   147→        self,
   148→        input_size: int = 128,
   149→        hidden_size: int = 64,
   150→        forecast_horizon: int = 7,
   151→        dropout: float = 0.2,
   152→        n_layers: int = 2
   153→    ):
   154→        super().__init__()
   155→        self.forecast_horizon = forecast_horizon
   156→
   157→        if n_layers == 1:
   158→            self.network = nn.Linear(input_size, forecast_horizon)
   159→        elif n_layers == 2:
   160→            self.network = nn.Sequential(
   161→                nn.Linear(input_size, hidden_size),
   162→                nn.ReLU(),
   163→                nn.Dropout(dropout),
   164→                nn.Linear(hidden_size, forecast_horizon)
   165→            )
   166→        elif n_layers == 3:
   167→            self.network = nn.Sequential(
   168→                nn.Linear(input_size, hidden_size),
   169→                nn.ReLU(),
   170→                nn.Dropout(dropout),
   171→                nn.Linear(hidden_size, hidden_size // 2),
   172→                nn.ReLU(),
   173→                nn.Dropout(dropout),
   174→                nn.Linear(hidden_size // 2, forecast_horizon)
   175→            )
   176→        elif n_layers == 4:
   177→            self.network = nn.Sequential(
   178→                nn.Linear(input_size, hidden_size),
   179→                nn.ReLU(),
   180→                nn.Dropout(dropout),
   181→                nn.Linear(hidden_size, hidden_size),
   182→                nn.ReLU(),
   183→                nn.Dropout(dropout),
   184→                nn.Linear(hidden_size, hidden_size // 2),
   185→                nn.ReLU(),
   186→                nn.Dropout(dropout),
   187→                nn.Linear(hidden_size // 2, forecast_horizon)
   188→            )
   189→        else:
   190→            raise ValueError(f"n_layers must be 1-4, got {n_layers}")
   191→
   192→    def forward(
   193→        self,
   194→        encoder_output: torch.Tensor,
   195→        encoder_hidden: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
   196→    ) -> torch.Tensor:
   197→        """
   198→        Forward pass for temporal forecasting.
   199→
   200→        Args:
   201→            encoder_output: Encoder context (batch_size, input_size)
   202→            encoder_hidden: Unused, kept for interface compatibility
   203→
   204→        Returns:
   205→            Forecasted snow depths (batch_size, forecast_horizon)
   206→        """
   207→        return self.network(encoder_output)

   210→class TemporalHeadAutoregressive(nn.Module):
   211→    """
   212→    Alternative temporal head with autoregressive decoding.
   213→
   214→    Generates forecasts one step at a time, using previous
   215→    predictions as input.
   216→
   217→    Args:
   218→        input_size: Size of encoder output
   219→        hidden_size: Size of decoder hidden state
   220→        forecast_horizon: Number of days to forecast
   221→        dropout: Dropout probability
   222→    """
   223→
   224→    def __init__(
   225→        self,
   226→        input_size: int = 128,
   227→        hidden_size: int = 64,
   228→        forecast_horizon: int = 7,
   229→        dropout: float = 0.2
   230→    ):
   231→        super().__init__()
   232→
   233→        self.forecast_horizon = forecast_horizon
   234→        self.hidden_size = hidden_size
   235→
   236→        # Embedding for previous prediction
   237→        self.pred_embedding = nn.Linear(1, hidden_size)
   238→
   239→        # Combine encoder output with prediction embedding
   240→        self.combine = nn.Linear(input_size + hidden_size, hidden_size)
   241→
   242→        # GRU cell for autoregressive decoding
   243→        self.gru_cell = nn.GRUCell(hidden_size, hidden_size)
   244→
   245→        # Output projection
   246→        self.output = nn.Sequential(
   247→            nn.Linear(hidden_size, hidden_size // 2),
   248→            nn.ReLU(),
   249→            nn.Dropout(dropout),
   250→            nn.Linear(hidden_size // 2, 1)
   251→        )
   252→
   253→    def forward(
   254→        self,
   255→        encoder_output: torch.Tensor,
   256→        initial_snow: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
   257→    ) -> torch.Tensor:
   258→        """
   259→        Autoregressive forward pass.
   260→
   261→        Args:
   262→            encoder_output: Encoder context (batch_size, input_size)
   263→            initial_snow: Initial snow depth (batch_size, 1)
   264→
   265→        Returns:
   266→            Forecasted snow depths (batch_size, forecast_horizon)
   267→        """
   268→        batch_size = encoder_output.size(0)
   269→        device = encoder_output.device
   270→
   271→        # Initialize hidden state
   272→        hidden = torch.zeros(batch_size, self.hidden_size, device=device)
   273→
   274→        # Initialize prediction (use 0 if not provided)
   275→        if initial_snow is None:
   276→            prev_pred = torch.zeros(batch_size, 1, device=device)
   277→        else:
   278→            prev_pred = initial_snow
   279→
   280→        predictions = []
   281→
   282→        for t in range(self.forecast_horizon):
   283→            # Embed previous prediction
   284→            pred_emb = self.pred_embedding(prev_pred)
   285→
   286→            # Combine with encoder output
   287→            combined = torch.cat([encoder_output, pred_emb], dim=-1)
   288→            combined = self.combine(combined)
   289→
   290→            # GRU step
   291→            hidden = self.gru_cell(combined, hidden)
   292→
   293→            # Generate prediction (clamp to non-negative: snow depth >= 0)
   294→            pred = self.output(hidden)
   295→            pred = torch.clamp(pred, min=0)
   296→            predictions.append(pred)
   297→
   298→            # Use prediction for next step
   299→            prev_pred = pred
   300→
   301→        # Stack predictions
   302→        predictions = torch.cat(predictions, dim=-1)  # (batch, forecast_horizon)
   303→
   304→        return predictions
   305→
   306→
   307→class AnomalyHead(nn.Module):
   308→    """
   309→    Head D: Anomaly/extreme event detection.
   310→
   311→    Binary classification head for detecting extreme snow events
   312→    (heavy snowfall, rapid melt, rain-on-snow).
   313→
   314→    Args:
   315→        input_size: Size of encoder output
   316→        hidden_size: Size of hidden layer
   317→        dropout: Dropout probability
   318→    """
   319→
   320→    def __init__(
   321→        self,
   322→        input_size: int = 128,
   323→        hidden_size: int = 64,
   324→        dropout: float = 0.2
   325→    ):
   326→        super().__init__()
   327→
   328→        self.network = nn.Sequential(
   329→            nn.Linear(input_size, hidden_size),
   330→            nn.ReLU(),
   331→            nn.Dropout(dropout),
   332→            nn.Linear(hidden_size, hidden_size // 2),
   333→            nn.ReLU(),
   334→            nn.Dropout(dropout),
   335→            nn.Linear(hidden_size // 2, 1)
   336→        )
   337→
   338→    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
   339→        """
   340→        Forward pass.
   341→
   342→        Args:
   343→            x: Encoder output (batch_size, input_size)
   344→
   345→        Returns:
   346→            Anomaly logits (batch_size, 1)
   347→            Note: Returns raw logits, apply sigmoid for probabilities
   348→        """
   349→        return self.network(x)
   350→
   351→    def predict_proba(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
   352→        """Get probability of anomaly."""
   353→        logits = self.forward(x)
   354→        return torch.sigmoid(logits)
   355→

1→"""Loss functions for multi-task snow prediction."""
     2→
     3→import torch
     4→import torch.nn as nn
     5→from typing import Dict, Tuple, Optional
     6→
     7→
     8→class MultiTaskLoss(nn.Module):
     9→    """
    10→    Combined loss function for multi-task learning.
    11→
    12→    Computes weighted sum of task-specific losses:
    13→    L_total = lambda_A * L_A + lambda_B * L_B + lambda_D * L_D
    14→
    15→    Args:
    16→        lambda_A: Weight for spatial prediction loss
    17→        lambda_B: Weight for temporal prediction loss
    18→        lambda_D: Weight for anomaly detection loss
    19→        pos_weight: Positive class weight for anomaly detection (handles class imbalance)
    20→    """
    21→
    22→    def __init__(
    23→        self,
    24→        lambda_A: float = 1.0,
    25→        lambda_B: float = 1.0,
    26→        lambda_D: float = 0.3,
    27→        pos_weight: float = 10.0,
    28→        anomaly_loss_type: str = 'bce',
    29→        focal_alpha: float = 0.25,
    30→        focal_gamma: float = 2.0
    31→    ):
    32→        super().__init__()
    33→
    34→        self.lambda_A = lambda_A
    35→        self.lambda_B = lambda_B
    36→        self.lambda_D = lambda_D
    37→
    38→        # Loss functions for each task
    39→        self.loss_A = nn.MSELoss()
    40→        self.loss_B = nn.MSELoss()
    41→
    42→        if anomaly_loss_type == 'focal':
    43→            self.loss_D = FocalLoss(alpha=focal_alpha, gamma=focal_gamma)
    44→        else:
    45→            self.loss_D = nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss(
    46→                pos_weight=torch.tensor([pos_weight])
    47→            )
    48→
    49→    def forward(
    50→        self,
    51→        predictions: Dict[str, torch.Tensor],
    52→        targets: Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]
    53→    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, Dict[str, torch.Tensor]]:
    54→        """
    55→        Compute combined multi-task loss.
    56→
    57→        Args:
    58→            predictions: Dict with 'A', 'B', 'D' predictions
    59→            targets: Tuple of (target_A, target_B, target_D)
    60→
    61→        Returns:
    62→            total_loss: Combined weighted loss
    63→            loss_dict: Dictionary of individual losses
    64→        """
    65→        target_A, target_B, target_D = targets
    66→
    67→        # Move pos_weight to correct device if needed (BCE only, not focal)
    68→        if hasattr(self.loss_D, 'pos_weight') and self.loss_D.pos_weight.device != predictions['D'].device:
    69→            self.loss_D.pos_weight = self.loss_D.pos_weight.to(predictions['D'].device)
    70→
    71→        # Compute individual losses
    72→        loss_A = self.loss_A(predictions['A'], target_A)
    73→        loss_B = self.loss_B(predictions['B'], target_B)
    74→        loss_D = self.loss_D(predictions['D'], target_D)
    75→
    76→        # Combined loss
    77→        total_loss = (
    78→            self.lambda_A * loss_A +
    79→            self.lambda_B * loss_B +
    80→            self.lambda_D * loss_D
    81→        )
    82→
    83→        loss_dict = {
    84→            'total': total_loss,
    85→            'spatial': loss_A,
    86→            'temporal': loss_B,
    87→            'anomaly': loss_D
    88→        }
    89→
    90→        return total_loss, loss_dict
    91→
    92→
    93→class UncertaintyWeightedMultiTaskLoss(nn.Module):
    94→    """
    95→    Uncertainty-weighted multi-task loss (Kendall et al., CVPR 2018).
    96→
    97→    Learns per-task log-variance parameters that automatically balance
    98→    task losses based on their magnitudes. Replaces manual lambda tuning.
    99→
   100→    L = exp(-s_A)*L_A + s_A + exp(-s_B)*L_B + s_B + exp(-s_D)*L_D + s_D
   101→    where s_i = log(sigma^2_i) are learnable parameters.
   102→
   103→    Args:
   104→        pos_weight: Positive class weight for anomaly BCE loss
   105→        init_log_var_A: Initial log-variance for spatial (default 0.0)
   106→        init_log_var_B: Initial log-variance for temporal (default 0.0)
   107→        init_log_var_D: Initial log-variance for anomaly (default 0.0)
   108→        log_var_min: Minimum clamp for log-variance (default None = no clamp)
   109→        log_var_max: Maximum clamp for log-variance (default None = no clamp)
   110→    """
   111→
   112→    def __init__(
   113→        self,
   114→        pos_weight: float = 25.0,
   115→        init_log_var_A: float = 0.0,
   116→        init_log_var_B: float = 0.0,
   117→        init_log_var_D: float = 0.0,
   118→        log_var_min: Optional[float] = None,
   119→        log_var_max: Optional[float] = None
   120→    ):
   121→        super().__init__()
   122→        # Learnable log-variance params with magnitude-aware initialization
   123→        self.log_var_A = nn.Parameter(torch.tensor([init_log_var_A]))
   124→        self.log_var_B = nn.Parameter(torch.tensor([init_log_var_B]))
   125→        self.log_var_D = nn.Parameter(torch.tensor([init_log_var_D]))
   126→
   127→        self.log_var_min = log_var_min
   128→        self.log_var_max = log_var_max
   129→
   130→        self.loss_A = nn.MSELoss()
   131→        self.loss_B = nn.MSELoss()
   132→        self.loss_D = nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss(
   133→            pos_weight=torch.tensor([pos_weight])
   134→        )
   135→
   136→    def _clamp_log_vars(self):
   137→        """Clamp log-variance parameters to prevent collapse or explosion."""
   138→        if self.log_var_min is not None or self.log_var_max is not None:
   139→            lo = self.log_var_min if self.log_var_min is not None else float('-inf')
   140→            hi = self.log_var_max if self.log_var_max is not None else float('inf')
   141→            return (
   142→                self.log_var_A.clamp(lo, hi),
   143→                self.log_var_B.clamp(lo, hi),
   144→                self.log_var_D.clamp(lo, hi)
   145→            )
   146→        return self.log_var_A, self.log_var_B, self.log_var_D
   147→
   148→    def forward(
   149→        self,
   150→        predictions: Dict[str, torch.Tensor],
   151→        targets: Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]
   152→    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, Dict[str, torch.Tensor]]:
   153→        target_A, target_B, target_D = targets
   154→
   155→        # Device handling for pos_weight
   156→        if self.loss_D.pos_weight.device != predictions['D'].device:
   157→            self.loss_D.pos_weight = self.loss_D.pos_weight.to(predictions['D'].device)
   158→
   159→        # Raw per-task losses
   160→        loss_A = self.loss_A(predictions['A'], target_A)
   161→        loss_B = self.loss_B(predictions['B'], target_B)
   162→        loss_D = self.loss_D(predictions['D'], target_D)
   163→
   164→        # Get (possibly clamped) log-variances
   165→        lv_A, lv_B, lv_D = self._clamp_log_vars()
   166→
   167→        # Uncertainty-weighted combination
   168→        precision_A = torch.exp(-lv_A)
   169→        precision_B = torch.exp(-lv_B)
   170→        precision_D = torch.exp(-lv_D)
   171→
   172→        total = (precision_A * loss_A + lv_A +
   173→                 precision_B * loss_B + lv_B +
   174→                 precision_D * loss_D + lv_D).squeeze()
   175→
   176→        loss_dict = {
   177→            'total': total,
   178→            'spatial': loss_A,
   179→            'temporal': loss_B,
   180→            'anomaly': loss_D,
   181→            'weight_A': precision_A,
   182→            'weight_B': precision_B,
   183→            'weight_D': precision_D
   184→        }
   185→
   186→        return total, loss_dict
   187→
   188→
   189→class SpatialLoss(nn.Module):
   190→    """Loss for spatial (Head A) prediction."""
   191→
   192→    def __init__(self, reduction: str = 'mean'):
   193→        super().__init__()
   194→        self.mse = nn.MSELoss(reduction=reduction)
   195→
   196→    def forward(
   197→        self,
   198→        predictions: torch.Tensor,
   199→        targets: torch.Tensor
   200→    ) -> torch.Tensor:
   201→        return self.mse(predictions, targets)
   202→
   203→
   204→class TemporalLoss(nn.Module):
   205→    """
   206→    Loss for temporal (Head B) forecasting.
   207→
   208→    Optionally weights later timesteps more heavily.
   209→
   210→    Args:
   211→        forecast_horizon: Number of forecast steps
   212→        weight_increase: If True, weight later predictions more
   213→    """
   214→
   215→    def __init__(
   216→        self,
   217→        forecast_horizon: int = 7,
   218→        weight_increase: bool = False
   219→    ):
   220→        super().__init__()
   221→        self.forecast_horizon = forecast_horizon
   222→
   223→        if weight_increase:
   224→            # Linearly increasing weights
   225→            weights = torch.arange(1, forecast_horizon + 1, dtype=torch.float32)
   226→            weights = weights / weights.sum() * forecast_horizon
   227→            self.register_buffer('weights', weights)
   228→        else:
   229→            self.register_buffer('weights', torch.ones(forecast_horizon))
   230→
   231→    def forward(
   232→        self,
   233→        predictions: torch.Tensor,
   234→        targets: torch.Tensor
   235→    ) -> torch.Tensor:
   236→        """
   237→        Compute weighted MSE loss over forecast horizon.
   238→
   239→        Args:
   240→            predictions: (batch_size, forecast_horizon)
   241→            targets: (batch_size, forecast_horizon)
   242→
   243→        Returns:
   244→            Weighted MSE loss
   245→        """
   246→        # Move weights to correct device
   247→        if self.weights.device != predictions.device:
   248→            self.weights = self.weights.to(predictions.device)
   249→
   250→        # Compute per-timestep squared error
   251→        sq_error = (predictions - targets) ** 2  # (batch, horizon)
   252→
   253→        # Apply weights
   254→        weighted_sq_error = sq_error * self.weights.unsqueeze(0)
   255→
   256→        # Mean over batch and timesteps
   257→        return weighted_sq_error.mean()
   258→
   259→
   260→class AnomalyLoss(nn.Module):
   261→    """
   262→    Loss for anomaly (Head D) detection.
   263→
   264→    Binary cross-entropy with class weighting for imbalanced data.
   265→
   266→    Args:
   267→        pos_weight: Weight for positive (anomaly) class
   268→    """
   269→
   270→    def __init__(self, pos_weight: float = 10.0):
   271→        super().__init__()
   272→        self.bce = nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss(
   273→            pos_weight=torch.tensor([pos_weight])
   274→        )
   275→
   276→    def forward(
   277→        self,
   278→        predictions: torch.Tensor,
   279→        targets: torch.Tensor
   280→    ) -> torch.Tensor:
   281→        # Ensure pos_weight on correct device
   282→        if self.bce.pos_weight.device != predictions.device:
   283→            self.bce.pos_weight = self.bce.pos_weight.to(predictions.device)
   284→
   285→        return self.bce(predictions, targets)
   286→
   287→
   288→class FocalLoss(nn.Module):
   289→    """
   290→    Focal loss for handling class imbalance in anomaly detection.
   291→
   292→    Reduces loss for well-classified examples, focusing training
   293→    on hard examples.
   294→
   295→    Args:
   296→        alpha: Weighting factor for positive class
   297→        gamma: Focusing parameter (higher = more focus on hard examples)
   298→    """
   299→
   300→    def __init__(self, alpha: float = 0.25, gamma: float = 2.0):
   301→        super().__init__()
   302→        self.alpha = alpha
   303→        self.gamma = gamma
   304→
   305→    def forward(
   306→        self,
   307→        predictions: torch.Tensor,
   308→        targets: torch.Tensor
   309→    ) -> torch.Tensor:
   310→        """
   311→        Compute focal loss.
   312→
   313→        Args:
   314→            predictions: Logits (batch_size, 1)
   315→            targets: Binary labels (batch_size, 1)
   316→
   317→        Returns:
   318→            Focal loss value
   319→        """
   320→        # Get probabilities
   321→        probs = torch.sigmoid(predictions)
   322→
   323→        # Compute focal weight
   324→        pt = targets * probs + (1 - targets) * (1 - probs)
   325→        focal_weight = (1 - pt) ** self.gamma
   326→
   327→        # Compute alpha weight
   328→        alpha_weight = targets * self.alpha + (1 - targets) * (1 - self.alpha)
   329→
   330→        # Compute BCE
   331→        bce = nn.functional.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(
   332→            predictions, targets, reduction='none'
   333→        )
   334→
   335→        # Apply weights
   336→        focal_loss = alpha_weight * focal_weight * bce
   337→
   338→        return focal_loss.mean()

     2→
     3→import torch
     4→import torch.nn as nn
     5→from typing import Tuple, Optional, Dict
     6→
     7→from .encoder import SharedEncoder
     8→from .heads import SpatialHead, TemporalHead, TemporalHeadMLP, TemporalHeadAutoregressive, AnomalyHead
     9→

    11→class MultiTaskSnowModel(nn.Module):
    12→    """
    13→    Multi-task deep learning model for Nordic snow monitoring.
    14→
    15→    Combines a shared LSTM encoder with three task-specific heads:
    16→    - Head A (Spatial): Current snow depth prediction
    17→    - Head B (Temporal): 7-day snow depth forecast
    18→    - Head D (Anomaly): Extreme event detection
    19→
    20→    Args:
    21→        n_features: Number of input features
    22→        encoder_hidden: Encoder LSTM hidden size
    23→        encoder_layers: Number of encoder LSTM layers
    24→        n_heads: Number of attention heads
    25→        head_hidden: Hidden size for prediction heads
    26→        forecast_horizon: Number of days for temporal forecast
    27→        dropout: Dropout probability
    28→        bidirectional: Use bidirectional LSTM encoder
    29→        temporal_head_type: Type of temporal head ('lstm', 'mlp', 'autoregressive')
    30→        temporal_mlp_layers: Number of MLP layers for temporal head (1-4, only for mlp type)
    31→        use_residual: Use residual connection in encoder attention
    32→    """
    33→
    34→    def __init__(
    35→        self,
    36→        n_features: int = 9,
    37→        encoder_hidden: int = 128,
    38→        encoder_layers: int = 2,
    39→        n_heads: int = 8,
    40→        head_hidden: int = 64,
    41→        forecast_horizon: int = 7,
    42→        dropout: float = 0.2,
    43→        bidirectional: bool = False,
    44→        temporal_head_type: str = 'lstm',
    45→        temporal_mlp_layers: int = 2,
    46→        use_residual: bool = True
    47→    ):
    48→        super().__init__()
    49→
    50→        self.n_features = n_features
    51→        self.forecast_horizon = forecast_horizon
    52→
    53→        # Shared encoder
    54→        self.encoder = SharedEncoder(
    55→            n_features=n_features,
    56→            hidden_size=encoder_hidden,
    57→            num_layers=encoder_layers,
    58→            n_heads=n_heads,
    59→            dropout=dropout,
    60→            bidirectional=bidirectional,
    61→            use_residual=use_residual
    62→        )
    63→
    64→        encoder_output_size = self.encoder.get_output_size()
    65→
    66→        # Task-specific heads
    67→        self.head_A = SpatialHead(
    68→            input_size=encoder_output_size,
    69→            hidden_size=head_hidden,
    70→            dropout=dropout
    71→        )
    72→
    73→        if temporal_head_type == 'mlp':
    74→            self.head_B = TemporalHeadMLP(
    75→                input_size=encoder_output_size,
    76→                hidden_size=head_hidden,
    77→                forecast_horizon=forecast_horizon,
    78→                dropout=dropout,
    79→                n_layers=temporal_mlp_layers
    80→            )
    81→        elif temporal_head_type == 'autoregressive':
    82→            self.head_B = TemporalHeadAutoregressive(
    83→                input_size=encoder_output_size,
    84→                hidden_size=head_hidden,
    85→                forecast_horizon=forecast_horizon,
    86→                dropout=dropout
    87→            )
    88→        else:
    89→            self.head_B = TemporalHead(
    90→                input_size=encoder_output_size,
    91→                hidden_size=head_hidden,
    92→                forecast_horizon=forecast_horizon,
    93→                dropout=dropout
    94→            )
    95→
    96→        self.head_D = AnomalyHead(
    97→            input_size=encoder_output_size,
    98→            hidden_size=head_hidden,
    99→            dropout=dropout
   100→        )
   101→
   102→    def forward(
   103→        self,
   104→        x: torch.Tensor,
   105→        tasks: Optional[Tuple[str, ...]] = None
   106→    ) -> Dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
   107→        """
   108→        Forward pass through model.
   109→
   110→        Args:
   111→            x: Input tensor (batch_size, seq_len, n_features)
   112→            tasks: Optional tuple of tasks to compute ('A', 'B', 'D')
   113→                   If None, computes all tasks
   114→
   115→        Returns:
   116→            Dictionary with predictions:
   117→            - 'A': Spatial prediction (batch_size, 1)
   118→            - 'B': Temporal forecast (batch_size, forecast_horizon)
   119→            - 'D': Anomaly logits (batch_size, 1)
   120→        """
   121→        if tasks is None:
   122→            tasks = ('A', 'B', 'D')
   123→
   124→        # Encode input sequence
   125→        context, lstm_out = self.encoder(x)
   126→
   127→        outputs = {}
   128→
   129→        if 'A' in tasks:
   130→            outputs['A'] = self.head_A(context)
   131→
   132→        if 'B' in tasks:
   133→            outputs['B'] = self.head_B(context)
   134→
   135→        if 'D' in tasks:
   136→            outputs['D'] = self.head_D(context)
   137→
   138→        return outputs
   139→
   140→    def forward_spatial(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
   141→        """Forward pass for spatial prediction only."""
   142→        context, _ = self.encoder(x)
   143→        return self.head_A(context)
   144→
   145→    def forward_temporal(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
   146→        """Forward pass for temporal prediction only."""
   147→        context, _ = self.encoder(x)
   148→        return self.head_B(context)
   149→
   150→    def forward_anomaly(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
   151→        """Forward pass for anomaly detection only."""
   152→        context, _ = self.encoder(x)
   153→        return self.head_D(context)
   154→
   155→    def get_encoder_representation(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
   156→        """Get encoder representation for analysis."""
   157→        context, _ = self.encoder(x)
   158→        return context

   161→class SingleTaskModel(nn.Module):
   162→    """
   163→    Single-task baseline model for comparison.
   164→
   165→    Uses the same architecture as multi-task model but trained
   166→    on only one task.
   167→
   168→    Args:
   169→        task: Task to train ('spatial', 'temporal', 'anomaly')
   170→        n_features: Number of input features
   171→        encoder_hidden: Encoder hidden size
   172→        encoder_layers: Number of encoder layers
   173→        n_heads: Number of attention heads
   174→        head_hidden: Head hidden size
   175→        forecast_horizon: Forecast horizon for temporal task
   176→        dropout: Dropout probability
   177→        temporal_head_type: Type of temporal head
   178→        temporal_mlp_layers: Number of MLP layers for temporal head (1-4)
   179→        use_residual: Use residual connection in encoder attention
   180→    """
   181→
   182→    def __init__(
   183→        self,
   184→        task: str,
   185→        n_features: int = 9,
   186→        encoder_hidden: int = 128,
   187→        encoder_layers: int = 2,
   188→        n_heads: int = 8,
   189→        head_hidden: int = 64,
   190→        forecast_horizon: int = 7,
   191→        dropout: float = 0.2,
   192→        temporal_head_type: str = 'lstm',
   193→        temporal_mlp_layers: int = 2,
   194→        use_residual: bool = True
   195→    ):
   196→        super().__init__()
   197→
   198→        self.task = task
   199→        valid_tasks = ['spatial', 'temporal', 'anomaly']
   200→        if task not in valid_tasks:
   201→            raise ValueError(f"Task must be one of {valid_tasks}")
   202→
   203→        # Encoder
   204→        self.encoder = SharedEncoder(
   205→            n_features=n_features,
   206→            hidden_size=encoder_hidden,
   207→            num_layers=encoder_layers,
   208→            n_heads=n_heads,
   209→            dropout=dropout,
   210→            use_residual=use_residual
   211→        )
   212→
   213→        encoder_output_size = self.encoder.get_output_size()
   214→
   215→        # Single head based on task
   216→        if task == 'spatial':
   217→            self.head = SpatialHead(
   218→                input_size=encoder_output_size,
   219→                hidden_size=head_hidden,
   220→                dropout=dropout
   221→            )
   222→        elif task == 'temporal':
   223→            if temporal_head_type == 'mlp':
   224→                self.head = TemporalHeadMLP(
   225→                    input_size=encoder_output_size,
   226→                    hidden_size=head_hidden,
   227→                    forecast_horizon=forecast_horizon,
   228→                    dropout=dropout,
   229→                    n_layers=temporal_mlp_layers
   230→                )
   231→            elif temporal_head_type == 'autoregressive':
   232→                self.head = TemporalHeadAutoregressive(
   233→                    input_size=encoder_output_size,
   234→                    hidden_size=head_hidden,
   235→                    forecast_horizon=forecast_horizon,
   236→                    dropout=dropout
   237→                )
   238→            else:
   239→                self.head = TemporalHead(
   240→                    input_size=encoder_output_size,
   241→                    hidden_size=head_hidden,
   242→                    forecast_horizon=forecast_horizon,
   243→                    dropout=dropout
   244→                )
   245→        else:  # anomaly
   246→            self.head = AnomalyHead(
   247→                input_size=encoder_output_size,
   248→                hidden_size=head_hidden,
   249→                dropout=dropout
   250→            )
   251→
   252→    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
   253→        """Forward pass."""
   254→        context, _ = self.encoder(x)
   255→        return self.head(context)
   256→

     2→
     3→import numpy as np
     4→import pandas as pd
     5→from typing import Dict, Tuple, Optional, List
     6→from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
     7→from pathlib import Path
     8→import json
     9→import logging
    10→
    11→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    12→
    13→# Default feature sets
    14→FEATURES_ORIGINAL = [
    15→    'snow_depth', 'temperature', 'precipitation',
    16→    'wind_speed', 'humidity', 'day_sin', 'day_cos',
    17→    'latitude', 'elevation'
    18→]
    19→
    20→FEATURES_MESAN = [
    21→    'snow_depth_cm', 'temperature', 'precipitation',
    22→    'wind_speed', 'humidity', 'frozen_precip',
    23→    'visibility', 'cloud_cover',
    24→    'day_sin', 'day_cos', 'latitude', 'elevation'
    25→]
    26→
    27→# Column name mapping: MESAN pipeline uses snow_depth_cm,
    28→# model internally uses snow_depth
    29→SNOW_DEPTH_COL = 'snow_depth_cm'
    30→
    31→
    32→class SnowDataPreprocessor:
    33→    """
    34→    Preprocessor for SMHI snow monitoring data.
    35→
    36→    Handles:
    37→    - Missing value imputation
    38→    - Feature normalization
    39→    - Cyclical encoding for temporal features
    40→    - Per-station sequence creation for time series input
    41→    - Train/val/test splitting
    42→
    43→    Args:
    44→        seq_length: Length of input sequences (default 30 days)
    45→        forecast_horizon: Forecast horizon for temporal predictions (default 7 days)
    46→        features: List of feature names to use
    47→        snow_col: Name of the snow depth column (default 'snow_depth_cm')
    48→    """
    49→
    50→    def __init__(
    51→        self,
    52→        seq_length: int = 30,
    53→        forecast_horizon: int = 7,
    54→        features: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    55→        snow_col: str = SNOW_DEPTH_COL
    56→    ):
    57→        self.seq_length = seq_length
    58→        self.forecast_horizon = forecast_horizon
    59→        self.snow_col = snow_col
    60→
    61→        if features is None:
    62→            self.features = list(FEATURES_MESAN)
    63→        else:
    64→            self.features = features
    65→
    66→        self.scaler = StandardScaler()
    67→        self.fitted = False
    68→
    69→    def fit(self, df: pd.DataFrame) -> 'SnowDataPreprocessor':
    70→        """
    71→        Fit the preprocessor on training data.
    72→
    73→        Args:
    74→            df: Training DataFrame with required columns
    75→
    76→        Returns:
    77→            Self for method chaining
    78→        """
    79→        # Add cyclical day encoding if not present
    80→        df = self._add_cyclical_features(df)
    81→
    82→        # Fit scaler on feature columns
    83→        feature_cols = [c for c in self.features if c in df.columns]
    84→        self.scaler.fit(df[feature_cols].values)
    85→        self.fitted = True
    86→
    87→        return self
    88→
    89→    def transform(
    90→        self,
    91→        df: pd.DataFrame,
    92→        create_sequences: bool = True
    93→    ) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    94→        """
    95→        Transform data for model input.
    96→
    97→        Args:
    98→            df: DataFrame to transform
    99→            create_sequences: Whether to create sequences or return flat data
   100→
   101→        Returns:
   102→            Dictionary with 'input', 'target_A', 'target_B', 'target_D' arrays
   103→        """
   104→        if not self.fitted:
   105→            raise RuntimeError("Preprocessor must be fitted before transform")
   106→
   107→        # Add cyclical features
   108→        df = self._add_cyclical_features(df)
   109→
   110→        # Handle missing values
   111→        df = self._handle_missing_values(df)
   112→
   113→        # Normalize features
   114→        feature_cols = [c for c in self.features if c in df.columns]
   115→        normalized = self.scaler.transform(df[feature_cols].values)
   116→        df_normalized = df.copy()
   117→        df_normalized[feature_cols] = normalized
   118→
   119→        if create_sequences:
   120→            return self._create_sequences(df_normalized, df)
   121→        else:
   122→            return {
   123→                'features': normalized,
   124→                'snow_depth': df[self.snow_col].values,
   125→                'dates': df['date'].values if 'date' in df.columns else None
   126→            }
   127→
   128→    def fit_transform(
   129→        self,
   130→        df: pd.DataFrame,
   131→        create_sequences: bool = True
   132→    ) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
   133→        """Fit and transform in one step."""
   134→        self.fit(df)
   135→        return self.transform(df, create_sequences)
   136→
   137→    def _add_cyclical_features(self, df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
   138→        """Add cyclical encoding for day of year."""
   139→        df = df.copy()
   140→
   141→        if 'date' in df.columns:
   142→            dates = pd.to_datetime(df['date'])
   143→            day_of_year = dates.dt.dayofyear
   144→
   145→            df['day_sin'] = np.sin(2 * np.pi * day_of_year / 365)
   146→            df['day_cos'] = np.cos(2 * np.pi * day_of_year / 365)
   147→
   148→        return df
   149→
   150→    def _handle_missing_values(
   151→        self,
   152→        df: pd.DataFrame,
   153→        max_gap: int = 5
   154→    ) -> pd.DataFrame:
   155→        """
   156→        Handle missing values in the data.
   157→
   158→        Strategy:
   159→        - Linear interpolation for gaps < max_gap days
   160→        - Forward fill for isolated missing values
   161→        - Mark remaining as 0 (will be masked in model)
   162→        """
   163→        df = df.copy()
   164→
   165→        for col in self.features:
   166→            if col in df.columns:
   167→                # Linear interpolation for small gaps
   168→                df[col] = df[col].interpolate(
   169→                    method='linear',
   170→                    limit=max_gap,
   171→                    limit_direction='both'
   172→                )
   173→
   174→                # Forward fill remaining
   175→                df[col] = df[col].ffill()
   176→
   177→                # Backward fill any remaining at the start
   178→                df[col] = df[col].bfill()
   179→
   180→                # Fill any remaining with 0
   181→                df[col] = df[col].fillna(0)
   182→
   183→        return df
   184→
   185→    def _create_sequences(
   186→        self,
   187→        df_normalized: pd.DataFrame,
   188→        df_original: pd.DataFrame
   189→    ) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
   190→        """
   191→        Create per-station sequences for training.
   192→
   193→        Groups data by station_id (if present) and creates sequences
   194→        within each station's contiguous time series. Sequences never
   195→        cross station boundaries.
   196→
   197→        Returns:
   198→            Dictionary with input sequences and targets for all heads
   199→        """
   200→        feature_cols = [c for c in self.features if c in df_normalized.columns]
   201→
   202→        all_inputs = []
   203→        all_target_A = []
   204→        all_target_B = []
   205→        all_target_D = []
   206→
   207→        if 'station_id' in df_original.columns:
   208→            groups = df_original.groupby('station_id')
   209→        else:
   210→            groups = [('single', df_original)]
   211→
   212→        for station_id, group_orig in groups:
   213→            group_orig = group_orig.sort_values('date') if 'date' in group_orig.columns else group_orig
   214→            idx = group_orig.index
   215→
   216→            group_norm = df_normalized.loc[idx]
   217→            features = group_norm[feature_cols].values
   218→            snow_depth = group_orig[self.snow_col].values
   219→
   220→            min_length = self.seq_length + self.forecast_horizon + 1
   221→            if len(features) < min_length:
   222→                continue
   223→
   224→            anomaly_labels = self._create_anomaly_labels(group_orig)
   225→            n_samples = len(features) - self.seq_length - self.forecast_horizon
   226→
   227→            for i in range(n_samples):
   228→                all_inputs.append(features[i:i + self.seq_length])
   229→                all_target_A.append(snow_depth[i + self.seq_length - 1])
   230→                all_target_B.append(snow_depth[i + self.seq_length:i + self.seq_length + self.forecast_horizon])
   231→                all_target_D.append(anomaly_labels[i + self.seq_length])
   232→
   233→        if not all_inputs:
   234→            raise ValueError(
   235→                f"No valid sequences created. Need at least "
   236→                f"{self.seq_length + self.forecast_horizon + 1} consecutive days per station."
   237→            )
   238→
   239→        logger.info(f"Created {len(all_inputs):,} sequences from "
   240→                     f"{len(set(df_original['station_id'])) if 'station_id' in df_original.columns else 1} stations")
   241→
   242→        return {
   243→            'input': np.array(all_inputs, dtype=np.float32),
   244→            'target_A': np.array(all_target_A, dtype=np.float32),
   245→            'target_B': np.array(all_target_B, dtype=np.float32),
   246→            'target_D': np.array(all_target_D, dtype=np.float32)
   247→        }
   248→
   249→    def _create_anomaly_labels(self, df: pd.DataFrame) -> np.ndarray:
   250→        """
   251→        Create binary labels for extreme snow events.
   252→
   253→        Uses MESAN-specific features when available:
   254→        - Heavy snowfall: snow increase > 20 cm/day OR frozen_precip > 5 cm
   255→        - Rapid melt: snow decrease > 5 cm/day for 3+ consecutive days
   256→        - Rain on snow: temp > 0 AND precip > 5 AND snow > 10 cm
   257→        """
   258→        snow = df[self.snow_col].values
   259→        labels = np.zeros(len(df), dtype=np.float32)
   260→
   261→        # Snow depth daily change
   262→        snow_change = np.diff(snow, prepend=snow[0])
   263→
   264→        # Heavy snowfall (> 20 cm increase in 1 day)
   265→        labels[snow_change > 20] = 1.0
   266→
   267→        # Heavy frozen precipitation from MESAN (> 5 cm in 24h)
   268→        if 'frozen_precip' in df.columns:
   269→            frozen = df['frozen_precip'].values
   270→            labels[frozen > 5.0] = 1.0
   271→
   272→        # Rapid melt (> 5 cm/day decrease for 3+ consecutive days)
   273→        for i in range(3, len(snow)):
   274→            if np.all(snow_change[i-2:i+1] < -5):
   275→                labels[i] = 1.0
   276→
   277→        # Rain on snow (temp > 0, significant precip, existing snow cover)
   278→        if 'temperature' in df.columns and 'precipitation' in df.columns:
   279→            temp = df['temperature'].values
   280→            precip = df['precipitation'].values
   281→            rain_on_snow = (precip > 5) & (temp > 0) & (snow > 10)
   282→            labels[rain_on_snow] = 1.0
   283→
   284→        # Rapid melt detected via ground temperature (ground > 2C, snow decreasing)
   285→        if 'ground_temp' in df.columns:
   286→            ground_t = df['ground_temp'].values
   287→            warm_ground_melt = (ground_t > 2.0) & (snow_change < -5) & (snow > 10)
   288→            labels[warm_ground_melt] = 1.0
   289→
   290→        return labels
   291→
   292→    def save(self, path: str) -> None:
   293→        """Save preprocessor state to disk."""
   294→        path = Path(path)
   295→        path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   296→
   297→        # Save scaler
   298→        np.save(path / 'scaler_mean.npy', self.scaler.mean_)
   299→        np.save(path / 'scaler_scale.npy', self.scaler.scale_)
   300→
   301→        # Save config
   302→        config = {
   303→            'seq_length': self.seq_length,
   304→            'forecast_horizon': self.forecast_horizon,
   305→            'features': self.features,
   306→            'snow_col': self.snow_col,
   307→            'fitted': self.fitted
   308→        }
   309→        with open(path / 'config.json', 'w') as f:
   310→            json.dump(config, f)
   311→
   312→    @classmethod
   313→    def load(cls, path: str) -> 'SnowDataPreprocessor':
   314→        """Load preprocessor from disk."""
   315→        path = Path(path)
   316→
   317→        with open(path / 'config.json', 'r') as f:
   318→            config = json.load(f)
   319→
   320→        preprocessor = cls(
   321→            seq_length=config['seq_length'],
   322→            forecast_horizon=config['forecast_horizon'],
   323→            features=config['features'],
   324→            snow_col=config.get('snow_col', 'snow_depth_cm')
   325→        )
   326→
   327→        preprocessor.scaler.mean_ = np.load(path / 'scaler_mean.npy')
   328→        preprocessor.scaler.scale_ = np.load(path / 'scaler_scale.npy')
   329→        preprocessor.fitted = config['fitted']
   330→
   331→        return preprocessor
   332→
   333→
   334→def create_train_val_test_split(
   335→    df: pd.DataFrame,
   336→    train_years: Tuple[int, int] = (2015, 2022),
   337→    val_year: int = 2023,
   338→    test_year: int = 2024
   339→) -> Tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
   340→    """
   341→    Split data by year (temporal split to avoid data leakage).
   342→
   343→    Default years aligned with MESAN data availability (2015-2024).
   344→
   345→    Args:
   346→        df: DataFrame with 'date' column
   347→        train_years: Tuple of (start_year, end_year) for training
   348→        val_year: Validation year
   349→        test_year: Test year
   350→
   351→    Returns:
   352→        Tuple of (train_df, val_df, test_df)
   353→    """
   354→    df = df.copy()
   355→    df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'])
   356→    df['year'] = df['date'].dt.year
   357→
   358→    train_df = df[(df['year'] >= train_years[0]) & (df['year'] <= train_years[1])].copy()
   359→    val_df = df[df['year'] == val_year].copy()
   360→    test_df = df[df['year'] == test_year].copy()
   361→
   362→    # Remove year column
   363→    train_df = train_df.drop(columns=['year'])
   364→    val_df = val_df.drop(columns=['year'])
   365→    test_df = test_df.drop(columns=['year'])
   366→
   367→    logger.info(f"Train: {len(train_df):,} rows ({train_years[0]}-{train_years[1]})")
   368→    logger.info(f"Val:   {len(val_df):,} rows ({val_year})")
   369→    logger.info(f"Test:  {len(test_df):,} rows ({test_year})")
   370→
   371→    return train_df, val_df, test_df
   372→

    31→def load_data(config: dict) -> tuple:

    38→    Returns:

    61→        n_val = max(1, len(train_data['input']) // 10)

    93→def _create_dummy_data(config: dict) -> tuple:

   100→    forecast_horizon = config['data']['forecast_horizon']

   102→    def generate_split(n_samples):
